summary: Iteration 168, backend only, narrow final QA. Checked the PNG compress_level=1 change (used only for reviewed full-res pages with page.rect.width>1600; smaller pages keep the original MuPDF PNG) and the time.sleep(.001) yield after each whole-page validation raster. All runs were in the foreground, in-process ASGI, against a disposable isolated DB (db_dropped=true, storage_puts=[], real_handles_left=[]) with LOCAL original PDFs behind a mocked storage GET. No live calls, no customer writes, no app code edits. RESULTS: bench 3/3 passed; pixel-fidelity + source-cache 17/17 passed (106 s; all 400 refs are RGB-exact to pre-163); whole-page smoke 3/3 passed (Jan 201 geometry checks / 26 pages / 26 pixmaps at 0.3 / 0 PNG encodes / 1 GET; invalid last ref and zero-pixel last ref both fail closed with no proof cached). PNG1 removes the PNG6 cold-CPU regression and is now faster than 164: Jan remaining-images crop_render CPU 10.76 s (164) / 14.76 s (166) -> 9.12 s (168), p50 156/203 -> 137 ms. Jan bytes are 58.28 MB / 46.75 MB -> 53.26 MB, which is -8.6% vs 164 and +13.9% vs 166. April output is byte-identical to 164 (7,587,192 B). The 1 ms yield fixed the event-loop tail: during the cold Jan preflight, /api/series max went 1028 ms (166) -> 135 ms (168), health p95 42.5 -> 1.0 ms, probes 2 -> 8. The cost is a small cold-preflight overhead: Jan 1131/1136 -> 1163 ms, Apr 330/328 -> 354 ms. The live deployer Cloudflare 520 is still UNRESOLVED (platform issue, not retested). Performance is NOT qualified for 500k users or global 4G; these numbers are server-side on the preview pod only.

minor.issue: The 1 ms yield adds about 25-30 ms per cold preflight (Jan +27..32 ms, Apr +24..26 ms vs 166). This is expected and bounded; warm is unaffected.

One max outlier of 400.6 ms (p95 122 ms is unchanged; earlier runs 140-166 ms). April does not use the PNG1 path (output is byte-identical), so this is most likely pod noise. It was a single run and was not repeated, as instructed.

Jan reviewed scanned images are 13.9% larger than with PNG6 (53.26 MB vs 46.75 MB for 78 images) but 8.6% smaller than 164 and use 15% less CPU than 164. The tradeoff is favourable vs both 164 and 166 for CPU. Bytes are a middle ground, not a minimum.
Cloudflare 520 on live is still UNRESOLVED (platform). Not retested, as instructed.

action_items: OK to publish from the backend perf/correctness standpoint for the tested scope. Keep PNG1 + 1 ms yield; a process pool is not needed because the yield measurably fixed the event-loop tail (series max 135 ms).
Still track the live Cloudflare 520 as an unresolved platform issue. Local passes do not cover it.
critical_code_review_comments: tejas_core._render_crop_png: the optimize_png gate uses page.rect.width>1600 in page points, not output pixels. This is correct for the current scanned Jan pages, but a future large-point vector page would also get PNG1. Harmless for fidelity; bytes may grow.
Pre-existing: the Jan reviewed crops output 1601 px wide (1 px over the 1600 target, from rounding with min(scale,1600/w)). Not a regression; 166 was the same.

validate_crop_pages renders all whole pages before reaching an out-of-range last ref (invalid page 999 fails after 26 rasters). It still fails closed with no proof cached. An optional cheap optimisation would be to geometry-check all refs first and then raster.
The derivative cache identity is bumped to render:5, so stale PNG6 entries are not served. Good.

test_iter166_wholepage_validation.py writes its EV file on teardown at a fixed path, so partial runs overwrite the 166 evidence. The tester backed it up and restored it. Consider an EV_OUT env override.
